rows.title: Motion authority is centralised on the safety supervisor
SAFE_STOP forces zero authorized motion
E_STOP_LATCHED requires explicit operator reset
Restricted-mode authorized motion is clamped to per-state limits
Fault injection alters inputs only; never sets safety state
Every supported fault class has a corresponding scenario
Every scenario run emits replayable event artefacts
Per-producer event ordering is monotonic in sim_time_ns
Mission runtime requests motion but never authorises it
Recovery is bounded and terminates in MISSION_ABORT
Keepout violations emit events and constrain mission behavior
Runtime diagnostics report subsystem health without owning safety
Operator E-stop transitions to E_STOP_LATCHED on the same tick
Full system launch must be runtime-verifiable
Required ROS topics must be discoverable and type-checked
TF tree must expose expected critical frames
Authorized command path must be verified at runtime
Live validation reports must distinguish status categories
ROS host prerequisites must be qualifiable
Runtime qualification runs must produce evidence artefacts
Runtime evidence must support baseline comparison
Qualification reports must distinguish static vs live runtime checks
Runtime regressions must be classified and reportable
Runtime and scenario evidence must be reconstructable into ordered incident timelines
Incident reports must distinguish direct evidence from inferred causality
Incident reports must identify missing and contradictory evidence
Foxglove replay hints must be generated without requiring Foxglove runtime installation
Incident index must support scenario, severity, outcome, and evidence-status review
Incident bundles must support replay review manifest generation
Replay review reports must distinguish missing, partial, static-only, and bag-backed evidence
Timeline markers must preserve evidence origin and confidence
Foxglove review artefacts must be generated without requiring Foxglove installation in unit tests
Live replay workflows must run only on self-hosted ROS / Gazebo runners
Replay bundles must support deterministic replay coverage analysis
Replay quality scoring must degrade honestly when replay artifacts are missing
Cross-incident replay comparisons must preserve evidence-origin distinctions
Operator review completion must never be inferred automatically
Replay analytics reports must distinguish static-only, missing-bag, partial, and bag-backed incidents
Source changes must be classified by impacted subsystem
Impacted subsystems must map to requirements and evidence artifacts where possible
Replay analytics deltas must be compared against an explicit baseline when available
Critical replay or safety evidence regressions must be gateable in CI
Reliability impact reports must distinguish warnings from blocking failures
Longitudinal aggregation must load every available reliability artefact deterministically
Replay-quality trends must be deterministic and labelled when history is insufficient
Reliability drift must be classified deterministically with documented rules
Governance health must roll up evidence, replay, CI, traceability, runtime, and review discipline
Evidence freshness must be reported, not enforced via wall-clock
Subsystem risk must aggregate frequency, severity, and recurrence
Coverage evolution must preserve evidence origin labels through aggregation
CI gate history must aggregate pass / warning / failure counts and gate volatility
Programme review reports must distinguish missing history from regression
Programme review CI workflow must not fail on missing live runtime evidence
Reviewer exports must provide CSV and JSONL outputs for the documented tables
Reviewer exports must preserve evidence-origin, static-only, and missing-bag status
Reviewer exports must include schemas and a manifest with row counts
Reviewer notebook scaffolding must not require ROS, Gazebo, Foxglove, or live runtime evidence
Reviewer exports must not claim safety certification or infer causality
Mission compiler must be deterministic and offline
Compiler must use bounded grammar templates and reject unsupported instructions
Compiler must preserve ambiguity honestly
Compiler must reject contradictory instructions
Compiler must enforce ODD validation
Compiler must classify mission risk deterministically
Compiler must produce a deterministic mission graph
Compiler must produce auditable explainability output
Compiler must emit a complete audit artefact
Compiler must produce replay-compatible metadata without claiming runtime execution
Self-hosted live runtime runs must validate runner prerequisites before executing
Live runtime evidence must include a bag manifest or explicit not_executed reason
Bag-backed status must require real bag artefacts and metadata
Live runtime evidence must integrate with downstream evidence pipelines
GitHub-hosted CI must not claim live runtime execution
Mission proposal providers must not execute or authorize robot motion
External LLM providers must remain disabled
Proposal outputs must be sanitized before compiler validation
Unsafe or ambiguous proposals must produce deterministic diagnostics
Proposal audits must preserve provider mode, sanitizer results, compiler diagnostics, and safety-boundary disclaimers
Skill requests compile only through deterministic templates
Generated motion code uses /cmd_vel_requested only
Unsupported, ambiguous, or unsafe requests produce deterministic diagnostics
Generated skills include safety reviews, diagnostics, and audit artifacts
Code-card metadata supports a future reviewer UI without adding frontend dependencies
